history.period: 9th century (about 1200 years old); renovated with help from Thiru Muruga Kirupananda Variyar in the modern era
history.summary: An ancient Murugan temple at Kumaravayalur (Vayalur), about 9-16 km west of Tiruchirappalli (sources vary; one says 8 km, others 14-16 km - verify). The moolavar is Lord Shiva (Adhinathar) with the Murugan shrine directly behind his sanctum. Vayalur is the FIRST holy place praised by saint Arunagirinathar in his Thirupugazh hymns, and the modern saint-scholar Kirupananda Variyar brought the temple to wider limelight through his speeches and writings. Legend says Murugan created the temple tank, Sakthi Theertham, with his vel (divine spear); dipping in it is believed to remove obstacles, cure ailments, and relieve Naga Dosham. The sthala viruksham is the Vanni tree. The temple is also known as the 'child adoption temple': couples adopt children here for a period believing it removes evil influences and defects, after which the children prosper. Kamika Agamam is followed for daily worship (six poojas a day). The temple is maintained by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious & Charitable Endowments Department. The CSV town 'Tiruchirappalli' is only approximately correct - the actual village is Vayalur (Kumaravayalur), documented here.

name: Vayalur Murugan Temple
town_description: Vayalur (Kumaravayalur) is a village on Vayalur Road west of Tiruchirappalli, between Uyyakondan Thirumalai (Karkkudi) and Somarasampettai, with the Uyyakondan river (a Cauvery tributary) flowing to its north. A small, green, temple-centric settlement famous for this Murugan temple.

travel.road: Vayalur Road from Tiruchirappalli; 10 km from the Central Bus Stand per one source (RJHF+H7W, Vayalur 620021); town buses run frequently from Central and Chathiram bus stands; the road is congested.

visitor_information.best_time: November to February. Thai Poosam, Panguni Uthiram and Vaikasi Visakam are the peak festival times.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 1:00 PM and 3:30 PM to 9:00 PM (multiple sources agree; one listing gives 5:30 AM to 8:30 PM); on festival days 4:00 AM to 1:00 PM and 3:30 PM to 11:00 PM. Six daily poojas: Ushakalam 6:00 AM, Kalasanthi 8:00 AM, Uchikalam 1:00 PM, Sayarakshai 5:00 PM, Irandam Kalam 7:30 PM, Arthajamam 9:00 PM.
